jobs.title: AI Red Team Engineer
jobs.description: **About Hamming** ----------------- Hamming is the security layer for voice and chat agents. Banks, health systems, and other enterprises are putting agents on phone lines where anyone can reach them, and where the agent can verify identity, read an account, and act. We attack those agents before criminals do, with the owner's permission, show what they fall for, and keep every fix tested on every release. We are one of the fastest engineering teams in the world. We prod deploy 4x / day. Devin Case Study Ranked \#1 Eng team OpenAI Dev Day 100billion token list **The role** ------------ Our researchers find the failure by hand. You make it happen a thousand times, against authorized targets, with evidence a customer can inspect, and again on every release. You own the harness: the runner that places calls and chat sessions, the evaluators that decide what a result means, and the replay that shows what changed. Thousands of concurrent calls, bounded, cancellable, observable. **What you'll do** ------------------ * **Build the attack harness.** A new technique is a new definition, not a new system. * **Generate useful variations.** Branch multi\-turn scenarios and voice conditions with the objective and conditions explicit. * **Make results trustworthy.** A successful attack, a refusal, an infrastructure failure, and an inconclusive result are distinguishable and inspectable. * **Make findings reproducible.** Scenario, configuration, model versions, tool events, outcomes, replay, and comparison. * **Keep fixes fixed.** Validated findings become regression tests that run on every change, with noise controlled. **What you'll bring** --------------------- * 3\+ years building backend services, async workers, or test infrastructure in Python or TypeScript, with the failure cases and the tests. * An adversarial mind: offensive tooling, CTFs, fuzzing, or a security project. The title does not matter. * Judgment about evidence: when an automated evaluator is enough and when a human has to look. * Idempotency, backpressure, observability, and limits that are enforced rather than documented. **Nice to have** ---------------- * Agent frameworks, voice or telephony systems, or LLM evaluation infrastructure * A security finding of your own, responsibly disclosed **How we work** --------------- We start with the customer problem, ship daily, and let evidence decide what comes next. Use AI tools to move faster and own the result. Direct, low ego, serious work. **Benefits and perks** ---------------------- * Competitive salary and meaningful equity * Health, dental, and vision coverage * Every frontier AI tool, fully paid, from day one * Conferences and events we sponsor * Flexible PTO * Offices in San Francisco and Austin; remote in the United States for most roles

jobs.title: AI Research Engineer
jobs.description: **Job Summary** We are accepting applications from individuals with backgrounds in deep learning, model research, and related areas of artificial intelligence to join our AI Research Engineer expert network for future independent project consideration. Potential projects involve carefully reviewing AI\-generated explanations and examples, evaluating research reasoning, and identifying where proposed answers are inaccurate, incomplete, or misleading. **Apply at https://work.atasc.ai/join?entry\=profile** **Duties** Depending on the scope of a future project, contributions may include: * Review AI\-generated explanations and examples involving deep learning, model architectures, training methods, and model research. * Evaluate research reasoning, including experimental assumptions, methods, supporting evidence, and conclusions. * Identify potential problems such as confounded experiments, data leakage, inappropriate baselines, inconsistent evaluation protocols, and unsupported performance claims. * Assess whether ablation studies and model comparisons isolate the intended variables and support the conclusions presented. * Provide clear feedback explaining what needs correction and why, including limitations affecting reproducibility or interpretation. * Suggest appropriate checks that could strengthen an answer without claiming experiments, tests, or results that have not been completed. **Experience** * Relevant background in deep learning, model research, machine learning experimentation, or related areas through professional work, research, relevant study, or practical projects. * Ability to explain your individual contributions, research decisions, and methods for checking your conclusions. * Strong analytical reasoning and attention to detail when examining experimental designs, model evaluations, and technical explanations. * Ability to communicate complex ideas clearly and identify missing information, uncontrolled variables, or misleading conclusions. Applicants at different career stages, including those with early\-career experience, are welcome. Describe your background and contributions honestly. A human reviewer evaluates your contributions and supporting evidence rather than assuming expertise from a job title. **Application Process** Applicants must be **18 or older**. Complete one profile application with your background, education, résumé, and responses to short expertise questions. Select all specialty areas that match your experience. For this specialty, the intake includes the following example: *An ablation claims a gain but changes the training data and evaluation protocol together. Explain how you would isolate variables, compare baselines, and report reproducibility limits.* Focus on your reasoning and proposed checks. Do not disclose confidential work or present unperformed experiments, tests, or outcomes as completed results. Profiles are reviewed before any later verification steps. Identity documents and a separate expertise file are not required to apply. Submitted evidence is not automatically considered verified. Regulated work requires a separate review of relevant credentials and the actual project scope. Approval means eligibility for future project matching, not professional licensure or guaranteed work. Any assignment depends on availability and agreed project terms. Compensation is agreed separately for each actual project. **This is an application for future project consideration, not a currently open paid assignment or funded vacancy.** Enrollment is free. Acceptance into the network does not guarantee assignments or earnings. Pay: $50\.00 \- $100\.00 per hour Work Location: Remote

jobs.title: Automation Engineer
jobs.description: If you thrive in fast paced environments, enjoy hands\-on problem solving, and want to make a measurable impact while working with modern automation and control systems, this role offers the challenge, autonomy, and growth opportunities to take your engineering career to the next level. In this role, you won’t just maintain systems—you’ll continuously improve them. You’ll apply your controls and automation knowledge to optimize preventive maintenance strategies, diagnose sophisticated issues, and enhance the performance of industry leading technologies such as conveyors, sortation systems, PLCs, scanners, vision systems, print\-and‑apply equipment, and SCADA platforms. Your work will directly influence uptime, safety, and operational excellence across mission critical facilities. What You’ll Do * Promote a safe working environment by complying with all applicable codes, regulations, governmental agencies, and company directives related to system operations and work safety. * Troubleshoot and modify software programs for material handling control systems, including PLC/PC controllers, Allen Bradley Controllogix/Compactlogix PLC platform and RSLogix 5000 software package. * Act as first level escalation in troubleshooting support, both on\-site and remotely, as well as during and after business hours, to repair all MHE controls software systems. Respond quickly to emergency situations, summoning assistance as needed. * Inspect systems to ensure the operation of equipment is within design capabilities and achieve operational conditions prescribed by the client. * Oversee scope of development, work request initiation, scheduling, and inspection of work performed by outside contractors, which includes proprietary work, licensed installations, upgrades, and maintenance and inspection of specialized systems. * Engineer process solutions and reliability improvement from concept to network implementation. * Monitor Industrial networks such as Ethernet, ControlNet, DeviceNet, Profibus, AS\-I, motor control systems, servo drives, frequency drives, and electrical distribution systems. * Monitor material handling equipment metrics and partner with site team to resolve equipment electrical problems that create performance deficiencies. * Proactively and effectively communicate with multiple stakeholders including, but not limited to, leadership, operations and the maintenance team on technical issues and project timelines and production impacts. * Facilitate analysis and reviews of failures and processes to provide recommendations to implement improvements or retraining to avoid future incidents. * Perform controls systems assessments to maintain and improve equipment reliability. * Clearly communicate technical issues, project timelines, and product impacts with site leadership, operations and maintenance teams. * Cultivate positive working relationships with our Client and the Operations Maintenance team members. * Perform other job\-related duties as needed or assigned. What You’ll Need * Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States without the need for visa sponsorship now or in the future. * Bachelor's Degree preferred with 2\-5 years of relevant experience. In lieu of a degree, a combination of experience and education may be considered. * Experience in at least two engineering design cycles including specification, component selection and programming. * 2\+ years of experience working with PLC programming, robotics system components and controls, and SCADA\-based monitoring and control systems. * Ability to be available and work in a flexible schedule/shift/work area, including weekends, nights, and/or holidays. * Ability to independently solve problems and carry out general instructions in standard situations with limited to no oversight. * Meet the physical requirements of this role including stooping, standing, walking, climbing stairs/ladders, and the ability to lift/carry heavy loads of 50 lbs. or more. * Ability to guide the exchange of sensitive, complicated, and difficult information, convey performance expectations, and handle problems. Preferred Qualifications * 2\+ years apprenticeship or equivalent experience in Control Systems troubleshooting/ programming. * Experience supporting a range of different conveyors and sortation systems. * Experience with robotic maintenance. * In\-depth knowledge of Microsoft Office products. Examples include Word, Excel, Outlook, etc. * Extensive organizational skills with a strong inquisitive mindset. * Advanced math skills. Ability to calculate difficult figures such as percentages, fractions, and other financial\-related calculations. You should be proficient in: * PLC Programming Experience * SCADA Experience

jobs.title: Azure Cloud Migration Engineer
jobs.description: We are seeking an experienced Lead Cloud Migration Engineer to support a large scale data center migration to Microsoft Azure for a healthcare payer organization. This role is a key contributor within the migration factory, responsible for executing repeatable migration activities across multiple waves, including building target environments, coordinating testing, executing cutovers, and managing post go live stabilization. The Lead Cloud Migration Engineer is the single technical authority for the Azure migration program. This is not a pure advisory or design role — you will design, build, validate, and execute. You will set technical standards, own the infrastructure\-as\-code delivery, lead cutover nights, and be accountable for the technical integrity of every migration from Wave 1 through Wave 4\. The right person brings both architectural depth (landing zone design, governance, security baselines) and hands\-on migration execution experience (Azure Migrate, ASR, Bicep, DNS cutover, rollback procedures). If you have only designed on whiteboards, this is not the right role. If you have only executed migrations without owning the architecture, this is not the right role. We need both. The ideal candidate is hands on, highly organized, and comfortable operating in structured, wave based migration programs within regulated healthcare environments (HIPAA/HITECH), where precision, communication, and operational rigor are critical. **Key Responsibilities** Design and own the Azure Landing Zone: hub\-and\-spoke network topology, ExpressRoute/VPN connectivity, NSG policy, DNS zones, subscription and management group hierarchy. Build and maintain the Bicep/ARM module library — the authoritative IaC for all migrated workloads. Every infrastructure component is code; no manual provisioning in production. Define and enforce naming conventions, tagging taxonomy, RBAC model, Azure Policy assignments, and resource lock strategy across all waves. Lead the technical discovery for each application — validate scope, document dependencies (shared SQL instances, integration endpoints, certificate chains, service accounts), and produce the migration design document. Own the Azure Migrate project: configure replication, monitor replication health, manage test failover cycles, and sign off on replication readiness before each approval block opens. Author and maintain the technical runbook (playbook) for every application cutover — step\-by\-step execution sequence, rollback triggers, decision points, and owner assignments. Lead cutover execution on production nights: execute the runbook, manage the technical team, make rollback decisions within the agreed time box, and confirm application health before declaring success. Validate DNS cutover, SSL/TLS certificate continuity, IP allowlist updates, firewall rule migration, and F5/load balancer reconfiguration as part of every cutover sequence. Manage shared SQL instance migrations — coordinate multi\-application joint cutovers, validate data integrity post\-migration (row counts, checksums, referential integrity). Support the Enterprise Architecture review gate in each approval block — produce the technical evidence package (network diagram, Bicep validated, security controls mapped, DR tested). Ensure every migrated workload meets BCDR requirements: Azure Backup policy, Azure Site Recovery replication (where applicable), RPO/RTO validation, and DR test evidence. Serve as the primary technical escalation point for the delivery team and the QA Engineer during non\-production testing, the approval block, and hypercare. Provide technical input to the CAB submission package — confirm the runbook is approved, Bicep is validated, all pre\-cutover checks are complete, and the rollback procedure is tested. Lead technical retrospectives after each wave — capture lessons learned, update the IaC library, refine the approval block evidence template, and communicate changes to the program team. Mentor junior cloud engineers on Bicep authoring, Azure Migrate configuration, and migration runbook structure. Manage the relationship with managed service provider, and application vendors where vendor involvement is required for migration. **Migration Factory Execution** Execute standardized migration factory processes across multiple application waves Build and configure target environments in Azure following approved landing zone and platform standards Support re hosted, re platformed, and lightly modernized applications Ensure readiness of infrastructure, middleware, and application dependencies prior to migration **Environment Build \& Readiness** Coordinate provisioning of compute, storage, networking, security, and access for target environments Validate environment readiness against migration and security checklists Partner with platform, network, security, and IAM teams to resolve blockers Ensure target environments meet performance, availability, and compliance requirements **Testing Coordination \& Validation** Coordinate and support application, integration, performance, and user acceptance testing (UAT) Validate connectivity to upstream and downstream dependencies (databases, APIs, batch jobs, vendors) Track test defects and coordinate remediation with application and infrastructure teams Ensure formal sign off prior to scheduled cutovers **Cutover \& Go Live Execution** * Execute application cutovers according to approved runbooks and schedules * Coordinate activities across application, infrastructure, network, security, and business teams * Support data validation, smoke testing, and functional verification post cutover * Ensure minimal disruption to business operations during go live events **Post Go Live Stabilization** * Own post go live (hypercare) support windows for migrated applications * Monitor application behavior and coordinate rapid issue resolution * Track and document post migration defects and lessons learned * Support formal transition to steady state operations upon stabilization **Documentation \& Reporting** * Contribute to migration runbooks, wave plans, and readiness artifacts * Maintain accurate migration status, risks, and issues * Provide input to continuous improvement of migration factory processes * Support audit and compliance documentation as required **Required Qualifications** * 15\+ years of experience supporting enterprise applications or infrastructure migrations * 10\+ years in cloud/infrastructure engineering, with a minimum of 5 years in Azure specifically (AWS/GCP experience does not substitute). * Led at least two end\-to\-end Azure data center migration programs — from landing zone design through production cutover and hypercare exit. * Personally executed production cutovers using Azure Migrate, including DNS cutover, replication failover, and post\-migration application validation. * Authored Bicep or ARM IaC for multi\-application Azure environments — not just used existing modules, but written them. * Migrated or managed SQL Server in Azure — shared instances, Always On configuration, or database migration using Azure Database Migration Service. * Worked in a regulated environment (HIPAA, PCI\-DSS, FedRAMP, or equivalent) — understands the difference between //'deployed in Azure//' and //'compliant in Azure//'.

Commissioning Qualification and Quality Support * Support factory and site acceptance testing, commissioning, and qualification of automated systems, including control logic, alarms, interlocks, data handling, and recovery functions. * Prepare or review user requirements, functional specifications, risk assessments, test protocols, and traceability documents in collaboration with Engineering, Quality, and Validation. * Support computerized system validation and applicable current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP), electronic records, electronic signatures, and data integrity requirements. * Assess automation changes, deviations, and corrective and preventive actions; document testing and maintain approved configurations and the validated state. * Serve as the automation subject matter expert during audits and inspections; support periodic system reviews and closure of identified gaps. Lifecycle Planning and Vendor Coordination * Develop automation obsolescence, upgrade, spare parts, and service support plans; identify risks from unsupported hardware, software, or unavailable source code. * Coordinate automation vendors and integrators, define scopes of work, review deliverables, and support budgets and procurement for controls projects. * Track recurring failures, automation downtime, backup and recovery readiness, and improvement actions; execute work under site safety and cleanroom requirements. Education and Experience * Bachelor’s degree in Electrical, Controls, Automation, Computer, Chemical, or Mechanical Engineering, or a related engineering discipline. * Minimum three (3\) years of relevant industrial automation or process controls experience, including hands\-on PLC and HMI work. * Experience in pharmaceutical, biologics, or other regulated manufacturing preferred; aseptic manufacturing and facility start\-up experience are desirable. * Experience with platforms such as Rockwell Automation or Siemens, BMS applications, and automation vendors or system integrators preferred. **What We Offer** * Competitive salary (DOE) * Health, dental, and vision insurance * Training and professional development * Stock option program participation Physical Requirements * Ability to sit, stand, and walk for extended periods. * Able to lift 25 pounds occasionally. * Ability to work in laboratories, cleanrooms, and manufacturing areas using required PPE. **We Are an Equal Opportunity Employer** OcyonBio provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by law. jobs.title: Early Career Research Engineer
jobs.description: **About us** ============ Parallel is a web infrastructure company. Our products are used by leading businesses in sales, marketing, insurance, and coding to build best\-in\-class AI agents with flexible and powerful programmatic access to the web. We've raised $230 million from Kleiner Perkins, Sequoia, Index Ventures, Spark Capital, Khosla Ventures, First Round, and Terrain to build the web for AIs. We're currently valued at $2 billion and we're forming a world\-class team of engineers, designers, marketers, sellers, researchers, and operational experts to achieve our mission. **About you** ============= You're a researcher who thinks like an engineer, or an engineer who thinks like a researcher. You've worked on information retrieval systems, embedding models, or neural ranking at scale, or you're deeply curious about the fundamental problems that emerge when training models to understand and serve billions of web documents. You thrive in the space between theory and production, where elegant solutions must also run efficiently on real infrastructure. You're comfortable reading papers from SIGIR and RecSys one day and debugging distributed training pipelines the next. **The role** ============ You'll design and train the models that power Parallel's APIs: the intelligence layer that helps AI agents find exactly what they need from the open web. This means tackling research problems that most labs encounter only at hyperscale: How do you train embedding models that capture semantic intent across diverse query types? How do you balance model expressiveness with sub\-second retrieval latency? How do you maintain index freshness when the web updates constantly, without rebuilding from scratch? Unlike traditional search engines built for human queries, you're building for AI agents that issue complex, multi\-hop queries and expect structured, programmatic responses. This is information retrieval reimagined for the LLM era, work that combines classical IR techniques with modern deep learning, applied at a scale that demands new solutions. **You might be a good fit if you have:** ======================================== * Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education, training, and professional experience * A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience * Years of experience required will correlated with the internal job level requirements for this position **Life at Parallel** ==================== Our team works **fully in\-person**, between our Palo Alto HQ and San Francisco office. We’re a flat, talent\-dense organization dedicated to solving technical and creative problems. We seek like\-minded individuals who share our passion for applying science, creativity, and consistency to big and complex problems with equally big outcomes. These are our values: * **Own customer impact:** It’s on us to ensure real\-world outcomes for our customers. * **Obsess over craft:** Perfect every detail because quality compounds. * **Accelerate change**: Ship fast, adapt faster, and move frontier ideas into production. * **Create win\-wins**: Creatively turn trade\-offs into upside. * **Make high\-conviction bets**: Try and fail. But succeed an unfair amount. **Compensation \& benefits** ============================ * Competitive salary * Generous equity * Visa sponsorships * 401K plans * Daily lunch \& office snacks * Dinner at the office * Unlimited vacation * Caltrain pass reimbursement Compensation Range: $150K \- $300K

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
jobs.description: **New York, NY · Full\-time · Hybrid (in office 3 days a week) · $150,000 \- $275,000 \+ equity** ***We’re deploying advanced agents into the real world to solve some of the biggest pain points in healthcare, and bringing the JOY back to healthcare by fixing the financial chaos behind it.*** Every year, healthcare practices fail to collect an estimated $125 billion in earned revenue. The money disappears into fragmented financial data, manual workflows, and opaque payer systems that don’t talk to one another. Often, these costs are passed on to patients through higher bills or rising health costs, and for many practices the losses are fatal. Joyful Health builds AI agents that take on insurers so providers get paid for the care they deliver. We didn’t start with a product. We spent ten months working as fractional CFOs for a dozen practices, doing the work alongside providers before we wrote the technology that automates it. We just announced our $22M Series A, led by CRV, with world\-class investors including the founders of MongoDB and KAYAK. Now we’re doubling our engineering team. **About the role** ------------------ We’re hiring one of our first Forward Deployed Engineers to build out the function. You’ll sit between our largest customers and our product, and your core job is to craft our agent harness to meet the real\-world needs of practices. You’ll design how our agents are orchestrated and train them on how each practice actually operates. To do that, you’ll embed with practices and their revenue cycle teams, learn how money moves through their systems, and build what gets them paid: agent workflows, data integrations, and custom tooling deployed on Joyful’s platform. This is an engineering role with a commercial edge, well suited to founders and future founders. You’ll ship production code, lead working sessions with customers, and help grow accounts. You’ll also turn what you learn in the field into what we build next. As a founding FDE, you’ll write the playbook: how we onboard customers, what gets reused, what goes back to the product, and eventually how we build the team. **What you’ll do** ------------------ * Own customer deployments end to end, from signed contract to a live, measurable result. Get each practice’s data flowing into Joyful, encode their payer rules and workflows into how our agent works, and keep tuning it as results come back. * Direct our agent and build account\-specific solutions quickly (agent logic, analyses, automations, dashboards), then work with engineering to fold the winners into the core platform. * Run working sessions with customers’ revenue cycle teams. Map their workflows, find where revenue slips through, and turn that into a scoped plan with clear outcomes. * Create SOPs and work closely with our revenue cycle specialists, turning what they learn from accounts into better agent behavior. * Partner with the account team on renewals and expansion, bringing the results and insights that show customers the value we deliver. Be the engineer customers trust. * Be the voice of the customer inside Joyful. Turn field insight into clear problem statements, specs and roadmap input. * Build the FDE function: deployment playbooks, reusable patterns, internal tooling, success metrics and, over time, helping grow the team. **We’d love to hear from you if…** ---------------------------------- * **You’re passionate about Joyful Health’s mission.** You want to solve real, pressing problems for providers and put them in control of their businesses. You naturally empathize with users and enjoy building with their needs in mind. * **You’re an engineer who loves being in front of customers.** You have 3\+ years of full\-time engineering experience in software, AI or data engineering, and you’ve moved toward customer\-facing work, whether as an FDE, a solutions or deployment engineer, or the engineer who always ended up on customer calls. * **You have strong technical execution.** You’re AI\-native and fluent in Python and SQL, comfortable across backend systems, data pipelines and APIs, and experienced integrating with messy third\-party systems. You’ve built hands\-on with LLMs and agents, from turning business rules into agent logic to debugging it when it gets things wrong. Side projects count. * **You think commercially.** You can find the business problem behind a feature request, scope work to the outcome that matters, and explain technical trade\-offs to a practice owner as easily as to an engineer. * **You have a radical sense of ownership.** You’ve shown clear growth in scope and responsibility, you thrive in ambiguity, and you can turn a single customer conversation into a plan and a working prototype. * **You have a low ego and a growth mindset**, and you’re excited to shape our engineering team and culture as an early team member. * **Education:** a degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. **Bonus points** * You’ve been a founder or an early engineer at a startup. * You have experience with healthcare data, revenue cycle management or payer workflows. It’s not required, but you’ll need to get deep fast: within weeks you’ll be reading remits and researching payer policy. * You’ve done the unglamorous data work that makes messy real\-world inputs usable. **Working at Joyful** --------------------- **Meaningful impact.** You’ll work on one of the most hair\-on\-fire problems providers face, so they can focus on caring for patients. **Autonomy and ownership.** As our founding FDE, you’ll shape the function and the company from the ground up. **Growth and learning.** You’ll get direct access to experienced founders and advisors, plus stipends for professional development courses and books. **Competitive compensation and equity.** $150K \- $275K base, plus strong equity in Joyful Health. **Be your best self.** Comprehensive healthcare benefits, unlimited PTO (with a minimum of 10 days off a year), flexibility, and regular team off\-sites and events. Please apply even if you don’t meet 100% of the criteria. Nobody checks every box every time, and we’d love to talk with you about how you see yourself growing into this role. We’re also very open to candidates with non\-traditional experience. *Joyful Health is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected characteristic.*

jobs.title: Full-Stack AI Engineer
jobs.description: **Full\-Stack AI Engineer — Liza** ================================== **About Liza** -------------- Liza Health is a Cambridge\-based startup building an AI\-enabled platform for modern primary care. Our bet is simple: primary care is the foundation of a healthy US health system, and AI finally makes it possible to rebuild and scale primary care from first principles instead of patching what's broken. Liza was co\-founded by Dr. Rushika Fernandopulle, a practicing physician who previously co\-founded Iora Health, the relationship\-based primary care company later acquired by One Medical and then Amazon, serial tech entrepreneur and investor Andy Palmer and healthcare serial entrepreneur Duncan Reece. We bring decades of experience redesigning care delivery together with a team that builds with frontier AI every day. We work alongside primary care practices to change how care is delivered: more time for relationships, less time on administrative burden, and patients who get the right care at the right time. If you want your engineering work to make care better for real patients and clinicians, this is the place. **The role** ------------ We're hiring AI Engineers who will design, build and ship the AI systems at the core of Liza's care model. You'll own problems end to end: sitting with clinicians and care teams to build real\-world healthcare applications for patients, clinicians and clinical operators. This is a generalist role by design. On any given week you might write a prompt and its eval suite, wire an agent into an EHR via FHIR, build a frontend feature for care coordinators, and develop healthcare data pipelines. We value curiosity, learning fast and shipping well. We don't care much about titles or hierarchy. The AI engineering bar here is the one set at the top AI labs: we A/B\-test agent changes in a harness, LLM judges score replies in production, and we review production traces every week. The difference is where the work lands: in the hands of patients and primary care teams across the US, helping real people live healthier lives while reducing overall healthcare costs. **What you'll do** ------------------ * Build production AI applications and agentic systems that support patients, clinicians and care teams across scheduling, intake, documentation, care coordination, outreach and clinical decision support. * Partner directly with patients, physicians, health coaches and operations staff to turn messy, real\-world workflows into clear technical requirements and measurable outcomes. * Work closely with our AI\-native design team to create experiences that are simple, efficient and effective for all of our users. * Design, test and iterate on prompts, context and tool definitions that shape how our models behave, and keep them versioned, reviewed and safe to change. * Define and run evaluations: build gold\-standard datasets with clinicians, write rubrics and automated graders, read transcripts for what the metrics miss, and set launch criteria before anything reaches a patient. * Integrate AI with our healthcare stack: our FHIR backend (Medplum), practice EHRs, HIE aggregators such as Metriport, HL7 interfaces, claims and scheduling systems, and our data platform. * Build with PHI, HIPAA, privacy, security and auditability in mind, including human\-review workflows and clear escalation paths for clinical risk. * Monitor systems in production and use error analysis, observability and user feedback to rapidly improve reliability, cost, latency and model selection. * Turn what we learn into reusable building blocks: shared eval harnesses, agent patterns, integration libraries and internal tools that make the whole team faster. **Who we're looking for** ------------------------- We want exceptional builders who believe in our mission and want to have a great time pursuing it. You'll fit right in if you are: * **A mission\-driven believer.** You think US healthcare can be dramatically better, that primary care is where that change starts, and that AI is the lever that makes it possible now. You want your work measured in better care, not just shipped features. * **A generalist.** You're comfortable across the stack and across problem types, from backend services and data pipelines to frontends, prompts and evals. You pick up new tools, domains and languages quickly, and you go wherever the problem is. * **An exceptional builder.** You take pride in shipping things people actually use at large scale and you have a track record of doing it. You move from idea to working prototype fast, then have the discipline to make it reliable. Startup experience is deeply appreciated at Liza. * **A strong teammate.** You do your best work on small, cross\-functional teams with clinicians, designers, operators and other engineers. You communicate clearly, share context generously, give and take direct feedback, and care more about the team winning than about who gets credit. * **Someone who has fun.** You bring c inevitable chaos of a startup, and building something meaningful with people you enjoy. * **Someone comfortable with ambiguity.** You can frame an unclear problem, make good calls with incomplete information, and own the outcome. No prior healthcare experience or clinical credentials are required. We'll teach you the domain; we're hiring for curiosity, judgment, craft and heart. **Essential AI skills** ----------------------- Strong candidates will be deep in several and conversant in all. * **Production LLM application engineering.** 5\+ years of software engineering (our stack is TypeScript end to end), with hands\-on experience shipping LLM\-powered products to real users at scale. * **Prompt and context engineering.** Designing, testing and optimizing system prompts, tool descriptions and retrieved context, and knowing each frontier model's strengths and failure modes; treating prompts as versioned, reviewed production code. * **Agents and tool use.** Building agentic workflows with function calling, multi\-step planning, memory and state management, and protocols like MCP, including multi\-agent systems with human oversight built in. * **Evaluation and error analysis.** Building datasets and rubrics with domain experts, LLM\-as\-a\-judge and automated graders, human rating workflows and regression detection, then reading transcripts, finding failure patterns and iterating until quality measurably improves. Evals are how we know a system is safe enough for patients. * **Retrieval and knowledge systems.** RAG pipelines, embeddings, structured knowledge and memory that let models reason reliably over large, messy, heterogeneous data such as longitudinal patient records. * **Full\-stack and systems breadth.** APIs, data infrastructure, web and mobile frontends, cloud deployment, CI/CD, containers and production observability. You can take a system from prototype to reliable production on your own. * **AI\-native development.** Fluency with coding agents and AI\-assisted workflows to multiply your own output. **Like to have** ---------------- * Experience with EHR and interoperability technologies such as Epic, Oracle Health (Cerner), athenahealth, HL7, FHIR, SMART, health information exchanges and data aggregators such as Metriport, Zus, Gorilla Health, Redox. * Exposure to primary care, value\-based care, care coordination or patient access workflows. * Experience fine\-tuning or post\-training models, or building data programs for supervised fine\-tuning and reinforcement learning. * Voice or multimodal AI experience, such as patient\-facing phone agents or ambient documentation. * Prior work as a forward\-deployed engineer, technical founder or early engineer at a startup. * Open\-source contributions, publications or side projects that show your craft. **How we work and what we offer** --------------------------------- * **Small, cross\-functional teams.** Engineers, clinicians, designers and operators work side by side. Every person has real ownership and direct impact on patients. * **One codebase, shared by everyone**. Our APIs, web and mobile apps, infrastructure and agents live in one TypeScript monorepo, and every engineer ships across all of it, with coding agents as everyday tools. * **Speed with rigor.** We prototype fast, test with real users early, and hold a high bar for safety and quality before anything reaches care. * **Fun is part of the job.** We take the mission seriously, not ourselves. Expect team lunches, hack days, celebrating wins together, and colleagues you'll genuinely enjoy. * **Location:** Cambridge, MA, with in\-person collaboration. Hybrid encouraged \- most people are in the office 2\-3 days/week but we are flexible especially after ramp up. * **Compensation:** Competitive salary and meaningful equity, plus comprehensive health, dental and vision benefits. Liza is an equal opportunity employer. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, which make us better at building care for everyone.

jobs.description: **Build the nervous system of modern manufacturing** ---------------------------------------------------- At Prysmian, we connect the world with advanced energy and telecom cable systems—spanning underground and submarine power transmission and distribution, as well as medium/low‑voltage solutions for construction and infrastructure. maintain clean, standard‑driven code. * Design HMIs using high‑performance (ISA‑101\) principles for clarity and speed. * Commission, integrate, and diagnose variable‑frequency drives (VFDs). * Lead SCADA architecture, dashboarding, historian integration, and reliable data acquisition. * Define data models and tag conventions; deliver dashboards, trends, and reports that guide operators, supervisors, and engineers. * Configure PLC‑SCADA communications, OPC UA, and historian structures. * Develop and maintain industrial networking: Ethernet/IP, managed switches, and segmentation tuned to plant needs. * Be the primary technical authority for SCADA/data; ensure changes are controlled and thoroughly documented. * Own automation upgrades, controls retrofits, and new installs; write control specs, review vendor designs, manage schedules/budgets/integration, and support ROI and cost‑benefit analyses. * Serve as escalation during downtime; build Maintenance troubleshooting capability; author standard work, playbooks, and training materials. * Advance continuous improvement across safety, quality, uptime, throughput, and scrap reduction. * Champion safety and compliance: electrical safety practices, arc‑flash documentation, safe work policies, and energy isolation. Contribute to cybersecurity and formal change management. ### **Qualifications** #### **Must‑haves** * BS in Electrical/Controls/Automation Engineering or related discipline. * 3\+ years of manufacturing controls experience. * Allen‑Bradley ControlLogix/CompactLogix and Studio 5000 proficiency; Ethernet/IP fluency. * HMI development/troubleshooting with FactoryTalk View, InTouch, Red Lion, Ignition, or similar. * Industrial networking fundamentals: IP addressing, managed switches, VLANs, and protocols. * VFD setup, tuning, and integration. * Ability to read/create/interpret electrical schematics, P\&IDs, and machine documentation. * Strong analytical, problem‑solving, and root‑cause skills. * Hands‑on presence on the plant floor; committed to safe work with control and power voltages/currents. #### **Nice‑to‑haves** * Historian experience: Wonderware, Ignition, OSI PI, or SQL‑backed systems. * SQL skills, data structures knowledge, and basic scripting (Python, VB, or similar). * Exposure to MES, OEE, downtime tracking, or broader manufacturing data systems. * Experience with ISA‑101 (HMI) and ISA‑18\.2 (alarm management) practices. * Leadership of automation projects and/or SCADA development in fast‑moving plants. ### **Work environment** * Frequent presence on the production floor among operating machinery. * Ability to move safely around manufacturing equipment. * Occasional extended hours or off‑shift response when necessary. ### **What’s in it for you** * Direct your plant’s SCADA and controls trajectory. * Visible, high‑impact outcomes on uptime and automation capability. * Backed by a supportive team and leadership modernizing automation and data systems. * A culture of continuous improvement and professional development.

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff - AI Infra Algorithm
jobs.description: **About NeuroSpark** NeuroSpark builds and operates a high\-performance AI inference platform that helps enterprises run large language models faster, cheaper, and at scale. Inference infrastructure is the foundation the entire AI application layer runs on — every AI product ultimately depends on how fast, how reliably, and how affordably models can serve their users. Our vision is to make that layer so efficient that compute is never the reason a good AI product fails.**About the Role** ------------------ Serving inference at scale is a scheduling problem. Requests arrive with wildly different shapes and latency expectations, GPUs are heterogeneous and expensive, and the difference between a platform that's fast and one that's economical usually comes down to how well work gets placed. That system is what you'll own. You'll design and build the scheduling and routing layer of our platform: how requests get admitted, prioritized, batched, and placed across a heterogeneous multi\-cloud GPU fleet, under real multi\-tenant load and real latency commitments. This is core\-systems work with a clean slate — you'll be making the foundational architectural decisions, not maintaining someone else's, and the quality of those decisions will show up directly in our margins and our customers' latency numbers. You'll work close to the metal and close to the math. Some days that means reasoning about queueing behavior and control loops on a whiteboard; other days it means profiling Go or Rust until the tail latency comes down. We're a small team, so you'll own systems end\-to\-end — design, implementation, rollout, and the production reality afterward.**Responsibilities** -------------------- * **Own the scheduling and routing layer** — design and build request admission, prioritization, batching, and placement across a heterogeneous GPU fleet spanning multiple clouds and accelerator types * **Engineer for latency and utilization at once** — drive down tail latency while driving up fleet utilization; these fight each other, and resolving that tension well is the job * **Model the system, not just code it** — apply queueing theory, control theory, and load\-shedding principles to make the platform behave predictably under bursty, multi\-tenant traffic * **Build multi\-tenant fairness and isolation** — ensure priority guarantees and SLO commitments hold when the fleet is saturated and customers are competing for the same capacity * **Own it in production** — instrument, observe, and debug distributed behavior in a live system; carry your designs through rollout and real\-world load * **Set the technical bar** — make foundational architecture decisions, write the design docs that anchor them, and raise the engineering standard of everyone around you **Qualifications** ------------------ This is an individual\-contributor role. We're looking for someone who has built systems like this before and can operate independently from the first week.* Substantial experience building and operating large\-scale distributed systems in production — you've owned something load\-bearing, not just contributed to it * Track record of designing core systems from zero to one, and living with the consequences of your architectural decisions * Hands\-on experience with scheduling, load balancing, request routing, or resource allocation systems * Strong systems fundamentals — operating systems, networking, concurrency — and the ability to reason quantitatively about system behavior using queueing theory, control theory, or similar * Fluency in a performance\-sensitive language (Go, Rust, or C\+\+), with the profiling and optimization instincts that come from actually chasing latency in production * Comfort with GPU infrastructure and LLM inference fundamentals — batching, KV cache behavior, throughput/latency tradeoffs; deep expertise here is a plus, but strong distributed\-systems judgment matters more * Clear technical writing — you can make a hard design decision legible to people who weren't in your head * An AI\-native way of working — you use AI tools daily and have your own view of how they change how infrastructure gets built * Mandarin proficiency is preferred for this role **Nice to have:** Kubernetes and multi\-cloud operations experience; open\-source contributions to inference, serving, or scheduling projects; experience operating GPU clusters at scale.**Why This Role** ----------------- * Ownership of a core system at the foundation of the platform, with the architectural latitude that comes with building it first * Meaningful equity — we expect the people who build the foundational systems to own a real piece of what they build * A small, high\-caliber team where the distance between a good idea and it running in production is measured in days **Compensation and Benefits** ----------------------------- The base salary range for this position is **$170,000 – $350,000 per year**. The range reflects the position across experience levels; actual base salary will be determined by job\-related knowledge, skills, experience, and work location, and may fall anywhere within the stated range. In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for equity in the company, along with medical, dental, and vision coverage, and other benefits.**Additional Information** -------------------------- We are able to sponsor H\-1B and other work visas for qualified candidates.

jobs.title: Principal AI Ops Engineer
jobs.description: **Built to set the gold standard for integrated AI infrastructure** Crux AI is a newly formed, U.S.\-based integrated AI infrastructure company created to remove the physical and operational constraints on consequential AI ambitions. Crux brings together power, high\-density data centers, TPU silicon, networking, orchestration software, and ongoing operations as one integrated system. Crux is being capitalized to plan every layer together, develop each one to demanding standards, and operate the whole system with efficiency and reliability. That gives hyperscalers, frontier AI labs, sovereign customers, enterprises, and AI\-native companies greater freedom to pursue the AI they are here to create. **WHAT YOU'LL DO** You will build the systems that let AI agents, not people, do most of the work of running Crux's TPU fleet. Reporting to our Director, AI Ops, you will be one of the first engineers on the team, writing the telemetry pipelines, correlation logic, and agents that detect, triage, and remediate failures across facilities, TPU hosts, the network, and the control plane before a customer notices. You will turn every runbook into code and every repeat incident into automation. This is a hands\-on engineering seat: you write and ship the software, then operate it in production. **In this role, you will:** * Build and own the telemetry and event pipeline that ties together power, cooling, TPU hosts, interconnect, and the control plane, with the correlation to tell a failing pump from a failing chip from a failing job. * Write AI agents that triage alerts, execute runbooks, drain and requeue workloads, and open hardware repair and RMA requests with Google, with every action logged, reversible, and measured. * Turn runbooks into code, so that every critical failure mode for the first build maps to a signal, an alert, an automated response, and an owner. * Build the guardrails that keep autonomous actions safe: blast\-radius limits, approval gates for high\-risk changes, and tested rollback paths. * Define and instrument SLOs and error budgets with Compute, Network Engineering, and Facility Operations, and build the views the team reviews every week. * Take part in on\-call and incident response, and drive postmortems that end in a fix that ships, not an action item that ages. * Measure the share of operational work that closes with zero human touch, and drive that number up release over release. **SIGNALS OF SUCCESS** **After 60 days in this role:** * Gained a complete understanding of the first\-build architecture, the failure modes that matter most, and the tooling in place today, and shipped a first working agent against a real, repeat failure. * Stood up the first version of the unified telemetry pipeline for the first build. * Adapted to a fast\-paced environment, triaging appropriately and continuously improving our function. **After 6 months:** * Taken the first Stage 1 cluster into production with automated detection and remediation in place for its top failure modes. * Shipped agents the team relies on every day, with a measured share of incidents resolved without human intervention. * Built the guardrails and audit trail that let the team trust autonomous actions in production. **After 1 year:** * Running automation across a multi\-site fleet where most repeat operational work executes autonomously, with measurable gains in availability, recovery time, and cost per chip. * Built a library of agents and runbooks\-as\-code that every new site inherits on day one. * Become a reason strong SRE and operations engineers choose Crux. **EXPERIENCES, ATTRIBUTES AND MINDSET THAT INDICATE A GOOD MATCH** **Experiences** * 10\+ years in software engineering, SRE, or production engineering for large\-scale infrastructure, including operating a fleet across many sites against hard SLAs. * Built and shipped AI\-driven operations systems in production, such as event correlation, anomaly detection, auto\-remediation, or agentic triage, with measurable results. * Strong software skills in Python or Go, and hands\-on experience with observability stacks (for example Prometheus or OpenTelemetry), Kubernetes, and large\-scale data pipelines. **Attributes** * You are outcome driven and hands\-on. You read the telemetry and write the agent yourself. This is a builder's seat, not a supervisory one. * You are close enough to the hardware to be useful. You understand how power, cooling, accelerators, and networks fail, not just how software does. * You have a high tolerance for ambiguity. You absorb ambiguity and navigate complexity rather than passing it along. **Mindset** * You are skeptical by default. "90% automated" is a hypothesis until it survives a bad night at a new site. You build the system that makes the next incident boring. * You deliver reliability through discipline, not heroics. jobs.title: Senior Applied AI Engineer (Forward Deployed) [NYC or SF]
jobs.description: **About Concurrence** ===================== Concurrence (formerly Amigo) is building the platform healthcare organizations use to build their own clinical AI agents. Our mission is to make excellent care accessible to every patient, not rationed by the limits of clinician time. Underneath our platform is the Health World Model, which unifies a health system’s data into a living, event\-level record of every patient’s care. On top of it, agents handle work across the patient journey, from intake and scheduling to medication management and clinical decision support. Our agents have supported more than 10 million patient encounters and are on track to grow tenfold this year. We run natively on Databricks, integrate with every major EHR, and are backed by Madrona, General Catalyst, and Optum Ventures. We’re about 35 people, working in person in New York and San Francisco. **About the role** ------------------ Applied AI is where Concurrence meets the real world. Our core engineering team builds the platform. We take it into health systems and build what each customer actually needs on top of it, as durable software that runs in production. As a Senior Applied AI Engineer, you own an entire customer use case, not a ticket or a slice of one. You take a deployment from brief to production. You make the architecture calls inside it, commit the timeline, and carry the outcome. Success isn't your agent staying up. It's the customer's number moving: more intake handled, fewer denials, faster time to billing close. Your work doesn't stop at one customer. We build custom first, on purpose. When the same shape shows up under two customers, you're the one who sees it, and the pattern you proved becomes part of the platform everyone builds on next. Applied AI runs ahead of the platform, not behind it. Our field work is the R\&D that decides what Concurrence becomes. **What you'll do** ------------------ * **Own a whole use case, end to end.** You run the build from the deployment brief to production and beyond. You set its internal design, commit the timelines, and ship at a bar that doesn't need anyone checking behind you. * **Build agent systems that hold up in clinical settings.** That means hierarchies of agents and skills rather than one monolith, and evals that measure distributions, not vibes. Nothing reaches a patient until it clears our safety floor and eval gate. * **Take on the integration reality.** EHRs, legacy systems, and customer data come in every shape. You find the path from what the customer has to what the platform needs. * **Make it compound.** You turn field\-proven patterns into first\-class platform capabilities. You also push proven work down from agent reasoning into deterministic data lookups, the move where twenty tool calls become one. That's how we grow without turning into a services shop. * **Push back early.** When a spec was never vetted, an integration isn't supported, or scope quietly changed mid\-build, you raise it before the build pays for it. * **Raise the people around you.** Mentor the engineers on your use case and help set how the team builds. Write documentation good enough that a coding agent or a new hire could pick up your work. **You might be a great fit if you** ----------------------------------- * Have shipped and owned complex production systems end to end, with real users depending on them. * Have real experience building with LLMs and agents in production, or the engineering depth to get there fast. * Treat non\-deterministic systems with rigor. You know three runs of an agent is a feeling, not evidence. * Hold the near term and the long term at once: what a decision costs now, and what it makes easier or harder for the team later. * Are comfortable in the room with customers and clinicians. You'd rather understand the workflow than wait for a perfect spec. * Care about craft. Your systems fail loudly to you before they fail to a customer, and they keep working while you're on vacation. **Nice to have** ---------------- * Healthcare experience: EHR integrations (Epic, Oracle Health, athenahealth), HL7, FHIR, or clinical workflows. * Experience with Databricks, voice agents, or forward deployed or customer engineering. * Time at an early\-stage startup. **Why this role** ----------------- * **Stakes.** Your work runs inside health systems and touches patient care. * **Ownership, early.** You own whole use cases from the start. At a 35\-person company, scope arrives fast. * **Leverage.** What you build in the field becomes the platform. Few roles let you shape the product this directly. * **A clear path.** Our Applied AI ladder runs from Senior to Staff or Tech Lead. You move up by the kind of work you can be trusted to own, not by how much you ship. * **A week built for deep work.** Collaborative in\-office sprints early in the week, a protected focus day on Thursday, and Friday to consolidate what we learned. **Benefits (available to Full\-Time Employees)** ================================================ **Health \& Wellness** ---------------------- * Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance * Daily catered lunch and dinner * Mental health support and wellness coaching * Flexible wellness stipend for fitness, therapy, or personal growth **Growth \& Development** ------------------------- * Annual learning budget for courses, books, or conferences * Conference attendance budget for professional development * Annual team offsite * Academic collaboration opportunities * Unlimited PTO **Our Core Values** =================== * **Patients Win, We Win** If patients aren't getting better care, we haven't earned the right to scale. Every internal decision gets pressure\-tested: does this make patients' lives better? If we can't draw the line, we question why we're doing it. * **High Standards, High Care** We hold a high bar for the team because patients are counting on us to get this right. But high standards only work with genuine investment in each other. You can take risks, admit mistakes, and challenge ideas. Not despite our standards, but because of them. * **Thoughtful Urgency** We move fast by default, but speed without judgment is recklessness. The discipline is knowing which decisions are reversible vs. not. In healthcare AI, the companies that win will be fast everywhere they can be and careful everywhere they must be. We build the muscle to do both. * **Intensely Measured** We instrument patient outcomes, provider ROI, system performance, and clinical accuracy. But data without action is surveillance. Every metric should have an owner, a threshold, and a response plan. If we're measuring something but never acting on it, we stop measuring it. **Who Builds With Us** ====================== * **Low ego:** Politics and territory don't interest you. The best ideas win, regardless of who has them. * **Direct:** You say the hard thing, challenge ideas openly, and commit fully once decided. * **High agency:** You thrive on trust rather than instruction. When you see something is broken, you fix it. jobs.title: Sr. Applied Machine Learning Engineer
jobs.description: **Job Title:** Sr. Applied Machine Learning Engineer **Team:** Engineering **Location:** Onsite \- Sawtelle (Between Santa Monica \& West LA) **Employment Type:** Full\-time, Salary, Exempt **Reports To:** Head of Engineering **ABOUT PLUG** -------------- Plug is an automotive fintech startup building the marketplace for electric vehicles. Consumers, dealers and commercial partners trade in, sell and auction used EVs on a platform built only for electric vehicles. Nothing in it is adapted from legacy automotive. Consumers get an instant cash offer in minutes, backed by data\-driven pricing and battery state\-of\-health analysis. Pickup, payment and title transfer are handled end to end. Franchise and independent dealers across the United States bid in real time on inventory sourced directly from these consumers, dealers and commercial partners. Sellers get a fast, fair exit, and dealers get a dedicated channel for sourcing used EV inventory. Plug was founded in 2023 and is led by former Tesla executives. It is backed by a $20M Series A from Lightspeed Venture Partners. We're building the most AI\-native startup team in Los Angeles: operators, engineers and ML researchers building the transaction rails for the fast\-growing used EV market. **WHY PLUG** ------------ * You'll help build the biggest infrastructure opportunity in automotive. * You'll work on a platform built only for EVs, with nothing adapted from legacy automotive. * You'll be part of an AI\-native company that is rethinking how work gets done. * You'll work directly with operators who have scaled multi\-billion\-dollar businesses in automotive, EV and marketplaces. * You'll work alongside a small, senior team, with high autonomy and a direct line to company outcomes. **THE OPPORTUNITY** ------------------- Every car on Plug starts with a number: what is this EV worth today, and what will a dealer pay for it tomorrow? Those numbers come from our models. They draw on auction results, market data, vehicle telematics and battery health. As volume grows, our models have to get more accurate, update faster, and be easier to trust and explain. You'll join our Intelligence team and work alongside our ML engineer and data team, who built the models behind pricing and battery health. Together you'll take those models further: sharper price and volume forecasts, battery state\-of\-health models built from telematics, and LLM pipelines that pull structured data out of vehicle, title and inspection documents. **WHAT YOU'LL DO** ------------------ * Work with the team to build, improve and run in production the models behind instant offers, auction pricing and sell\-through: valuation, price and volume forecasting, and demand signals. * Develop battery state\-of\-health and vehicle\-condition models from telematics and other time\-series data, which is often noisy, sparse or only partly labeled. * Take models through the full lifecycle together with the team: feature pipelines on our Snowflake/dbt stack, training, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, drift detection and retraining. * Evaluate models by statistical accuracy and by business outcomes such as offer acceptance, margin and arbitration rate, and help build the feedback loops that connect the two. * Bring in LLMs where they work better than traditional models, for example pulling structured data out of vehicle, title and inspection documents. Build the evaluations that show whether they hold up. * Strengthen how the team works as it grows: experiment tracking, model registry, reproducible training and code review for ML work. Share what you know, pair on hard problems, and learn from the people who know our data best. **WHAT YOU'LL BRING** --------------------- * 5\+ years building and shipping machine learning systems, with several models running in production that you supported well after launch, not just trained. * Strong Python, plus deep experience with at least one modern ML framework (PyTorch, scikit\-learn, XGBoost/LightGBM or similar). * Practical experience with forecasting, regression or pricing problems on tabular and time\-series data. * Solid grounding in statistics and experiment design: validation strategy, leakage, calibration, and knowing when a metric is lying to you. * Comfort with real\-world, messy data and strong SQL. Experience with a modern data stack (Snowflake, dbt or similar) is a plus. * Hands\-on experience building with LLMs: tool use, retrieval, structured output, and above all evaluation. * You work agent\-first. You've built your own tooling around coding agents, such as skills, MCP servers, custom workflows or evals. * A habit of writing things down: design docs, model cards and runbooks that others can pick up. * You enjoy being part of a small team: pairing, reviewing each other's work and sharing credit. * Comfort building inside systems other people designed. You can disagree, make your case and then ship the agreed plan. * High agency in an ambiguous, fast\-moving startup. You find the most valuable problem and ship against it without waiting for a perfect spec. * BS or MS in a quantitative field (computer science, statistics, engineering, physics, applied math) or equivalent experience. ### **Nice to have** * Experience with vehicle, marketplace, auction, lending or insurance pricing data. * Experience with sensor or telematics data, battery modeling or other physical\-systems data. * Experience with transfer learning, multi\-task learning or model distillation. * Experience with ML or LLM serving on a budget for latency and cost. **COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS** ----------------------------- **Annual salary:** $164,000 – $200,000 Salary ranges come from independent, third\-party benchmarking against national compensation data. Where an offer falls within the range depends on relevant experience, specialized skills, training and qualifications, current business needs and market conditions. We review ranges periodically and may adjust them as the market changes. ### **Benefits and perks** * Health, vision and dental insurance * 401(k) plan * 30 days of work from anywhere per calendar year * Daily lunch stipend * Equity (based on role and performance) * Unlimited PTO * Fully stocked kitchen * Dog\-friendly office * Ongoing opportunities for growth and development This is a full\-time, in\-person role based in our Los Angeles office in Sawtelle (between Santa Monica and West Los Angeles). We provide relocation assistance for candidates who need to move. Sponsorship is not available at this time. **Acknowledgments** Plug is an equal opportunity employer. We don’t discriminate based on race, color, religion, creed, national origin, ancestry, sex, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, pregnancy, age, marital status, military or veteran status, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by law. Plug will consider qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records in accordance with the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring and the California Fair Chance Act.

jobs.title: Staff Applied AI Engineer (Forward Deployed) [NYC or SF]
jobs.description: **About Concurrence** ===================== Concurrence (formerly Amigo) is building the platform healthcare organizations use to build their own clinical AI agents. Our mission is to make excellent care accessible to every patient, not rationed by the limits of clinician time. Underneath our platform is the Health World Model, which unifies a health system’s data into a living, event\-level record of every patient’s care. On top of it, agents handle work across the patient journey, from intake and scheduling to medication management and clinical decision support. Our agents have supported more than 10 million patient encounters and are on track to grow tenfold this year. We run natively on Databricks, integrate with every major EHR, and are backed by Madrona, General Catalyst, and Optum Ventures. We’re about 35 people, working in person in New York and San Francisco. **About the role** ------------------ Applied AI is where Concurrence meets the real world. Our core engineering team builds the platform. We take it into health systems and build what each customer actually needs on top of it, as durable software that runs in production. As a Staff Applied AI Engineer, you own our most complex customer use cases and set technical direction across deployments. You take a deployment from brief to production. You make the architecture calls inside it and across shared systems, commit the timeline, and carry the outcome. Success isn't your agent staying up. It's the customer's number moving: more intake handled, fewer denials, faster time to billing close. Your work doesn't stop at one customer. We build custom first, on purpose. When the same shape shows up under two customers, you're the one who sees it, and the pattern you proved becomes part of the platform everyone builds on next. Applied AI runs ahead of the platform, not behind it. Our field work is the R\&D that decides what Concurrence becomes. **What you'll do** ------------------ * **Own our most complex use cases, end to end.** You run the build from the deployment brief to production and beyond. You set technical direction within and across deployments, resolve tradeoffs with the platform team, commit the timelines, and stay hands\-on in the hardest parts of the build. * **Build agent systems that hold up in clinical settings.** That means hierarchies of agents and skills rather than one monolith, and evals that measure distributions, not vibes. Nothing reaches a patient until it clears our safety floor and eval gate. * **Take on the integration reality.** EHRs, legacy systems, and customer data come in every shape. You find the path from what the customer has to what the platform needs. * **Make it compound.** You turn field\-proven patterns into first\-class platform capabilities. You also push proven work down from agent reasoning into deterministic data lookups, the move where twenty tool calls become one. That's how we grow without turning into a services shop. * **Push back early.** When a spec was never vetted, an integration isn't supported, or scope quietly changed mid\-build, you raise it before the build pays for it. * **Raise the people around you.** Mentor engineers across deployments and help set the team's architecture and engineering standards. Write documentation good enough that a coding agent or a new hire could pick up your work. **You might be a great fit if you** ----------------------------------- * Have shipped and owned complex production systems end to end, with real users depending on them. * Have set technical direction across multiple projects or teams, and helped other engineers make sound architecture decisions. * Have real experience building with LLMs and agents in production, or the engineering depth to get there fast. * Treat non\-deterministic systems with rigor. You know three runs of an agent is a feeling, not evidence. * Hold the near term and the long term at once: what a decision costs now, and what it makes easier or harder for the team later. * Are comfortable in the room with customers and clinicians. You'd rather understand the workflow than wait for a perfect spec. * Care about craft. Your systems fail loudly to you before they fail to a customer, and they keep working while you're on vacation. **Nice to have** ---------------- * Healthcare experience: EHR integrations (Epic, Oracle Health, athenahealth), HL7, FHIR, or clinical workflows. * Experience with Databricks, voice agents, or forward deployed or customer engineering. * Time at an early\-stage startup. **Why this role** ----------------- * **Stakes.** Your work runs inside health systems and touches patient care. * **Ownership, early.** You own complex use cases and shared technical decisions from the start. At a 35\-person company, scope arrives fast. * **Leverage.** What you build in the field becomes the platform. Few roles let you shape the product this directly. * **Technical leadership.** Set direction across Applied AI while staying close to the code. Your impact grows through the decisions and patterns the whole team builds on. * **A week built for deep work.** Collaborative in\-office sprints early in the week, a protected focus day on Thursday, and Friday to consolidate what we learned. **Benefits (available to Full\-Time Employees)** ================================================ **Health \& Wellness** ---------------------- * Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance * Daily catered lunch and dinner * Mental health support and wellness coaching * Flexible wellness stipend for fitness, therapy, or personal growth **Growth \& Development** ------------------------- * Annual learning budget for courses, books, or conferences * Conference attendance budget for professional development * Annual team offsite * Academic collaboration opportunities * Unlimited PTO **Our Core Values** =================== * **Patients Win, We Win** If patients aren't getting better care, we haven't earned the right to scale. Every internal decision gets pressure\-tested: does this make patients' lives better? If we can't draw the line, we question why we're doing it. * **High Standards, High Care** We hold a high bar for the team because patients are counting on us to get this right. But high standards only work with genuine investment in each other. You can take risks, admit mistakes, and challenge ideas. Not despite our standards, but because of them. * **Thoughtful Urgency** We move fast by default, but speed without judgment is recklessness. The discipline is knowing which decisions are reversible vs. not. In healthcare AI, the companies that win will be fast everywhere they can be and careful everywhere they must be. We build the muscle to do both. * **Intensely Measured** We instrument patient outcomes, provider ROI, system performance, and clinical accuracy. But data without action is surveillance. Every metric should have an owner, a threshold, and a response plan. If we're measuring something but never acting on it, we stop measuring it. **Who Builds With Us** ====================== * **Low ego:** Politics and territory don't interest you. The best ideas win, regardless of who has them. * **Direct:** You say the hard thing, challenge ideas openly, and commit fully once decided. * **High agency:** You thrive on trust rather than instruction. When you see something is broken, you fix it. You don’t file tickets and wait for someone else. * **Bar of excellence:** You hold yourself to a bar most people wouldn't, and you want teammates who do the same. * **Skeptical:** You push back on rules that don’t make sense and question assumptions that haven’t earned their place. Compensation Range: $240K \- $300K

team members. * Enjoys mentoring and supporting the growth of junior staff. **Why AKS?** ------------ At AKS, we believe your work should support your life, not the other way around.
